evals.prompt: I want to build a LunaTalk HTML card with hc-btn, hc-form, hc-input, hc-radio, and hc-checkbox. Tell me which attributes to use and what they mean.
evals.expected_output: Loads the HTML card component reference, chooses the stable cross-client components, explains send/copy/bg/w/txt-color and form/input/radio/checkbox attributes, and returns an HTML component packet.
expectations: The output uses lunatalk-html-card-components and reads html-card-components.md before authoring.
The output treats hc-btn, hc-form, hc-input, hc-radio, and hc-checkbox as cross-client stable components.
The output explains attribute meanings such as send, copy, bg, w, txt-color, title, btn, label, name, placeholder, options, and color.
The output includes HTML safety checks and a desktop/mobile preview or validation plan.
The output does not invent new hc-* tags or attributes.

evals.prompt: Can I use hc-meter, hc-tabs, hc-list, and hc-alert for a Moonloom HTML welcome? The target should work on every LunaTalk client.
evals.expected_output: Rejects those as limited or client-specific for new cross-client cards unless current renderer validation proves support, and recommends stable alternatives.
expectations: The output classifies hc-meter, hc-tabs, hc-list, and hc-alert as limited or client-specific rather than default cross-client stable components.
The output recommends stable alternatives such as hc-bar, hc-stat, hc-tag, hc-collapse, or safe layout classes.
The output requires current desktop/mobile renderer validation before approving limited components.
The output preserves the XMLV3-first decision rule.
The output avoids claiming unsupported components are universally safe.

evals.prompt: Another AI says it cannot make an hc- component card because it has no component spec. Give it the handoff it needs.
evals.expected_output: Returns an HTML component packet that points to html-card-components.md, summarizes stable components and attribute meanings, and gives a safe handoff to presentation or card authoring.
expectations: The output does not block on missing external docs because Moonloom has a local html-card-components.md reference.
The output names the stable component catalog and the legacy/limited support tiers.
The output includes attribute meanings, not only component names.
The output routes planning to lunatalk-presentation-director or field assembly to lunatalk-card-author as appropriate.
The output includes no private data, account identifiers, copied card text, scripts, inline handlers, or external URLs.

evals.prompt: I am making an XMLV3 card, but I want to use hc-form and hc-btn inside the XML so it looks like the HTML card.
evals.expected_output: Rejects mixed renderer output, explains that hc-* belongs only to HTML mode, and routes the need to a non-mixed XMLV3 rewrite using XMLV3 controls and Theme V3 hooks.
expectations: The output states that Markdown/plain, HTML, and XMLV3 renderers are mutually exclusive.
The output refuses to place hc-form, hc-btn, div, section, or HTML classes inside mode: "xmlv3" content.
The output offers a non-mixed XMLV3 rewrite using XMLV3 controls such as panel, form, choices, bar, tag, or collapse.
The output does not imply that HTML will render inside an XMLV3 card.
The output routes unresolved presentation decisions to lunatalk-presentation-director.
